scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was right or wrong to call out the intern for throwing her banana peel into the bushes instead of the trash can. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, the setting: There's a sidewalk that's about 100 feet long, with trash cans at both ends. On one side, there are some low-growing evergreen shrubs. Recently, there have been a lot of flies in the area, so much that the building manager had to call an exterminator. This morning, I saw an intern walking to work, eating a banana. She was about three-quarters of the way down the sidewalk when she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. The trash can was only about 25 feet away, so it wasn't like she had to go out of her way to throw it away properly. I was a bit shocked and not fully caffeinated, so I blurted out, "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" with some hand gestures. She got defensive, saying it's organic and feeds the animals. I pointed out the peel was sitting on top of the bush and told her to pick it up. Instead, she cried, got the peel, and put it in the trash. I thought it was over, but later her boss confronted me, saying the intern had cried about how mean I was and couldn't do any work. I apologized, and we laughed about the absurdity, but now I'm wondering if I was over the top. So, was I right or wrong to call her out? Let's break it down. First, the action: Throwing banana peels into bushes instead of the trash. Is that littering? Well, technically, it's not the same as throwing a wrapper on the ground, but it's still leaving trash in a public area. The shrubs are part of the building's landscaping, so tossing peels there could be considered littering. Second, the context: There have been flies, so the building manager had to call an exterminator. That suggests that there's been an issue with waste attracting pests. Throwing organic waste into the bushes could contribute to that problem. Third, the response: I was upset because I saw someone littering, and I wanted her to dispose of it properly. But I was abrupt and not very nice about it. She took it personally and got upset, which led to her boss confronting me. So, was I right to call her out? On one hand, she was littering, and that's not good. On the other hand, I could have handled it more politely and calmly. Maybe I should have explained why it's important to throw it in the trash, especially given the fly issue, instead of just yelling at her. Also, her reaction was extreme. She cried and told her boss, which made the situation bigger than it needed to be. But that's her reaction, not necessarily my fault. I should take responsibility for how I approached her, though. In the end, I apologized, and we laughed it off, but I'm still wondering if I was AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) for calling her out. So, to sum up: She was littering, which is wrong. I called her out, but I was abrupt and not very nice. She overreacted, but that's her issue. I apologized, and we moved on. So, was I right or wrong? I think I was right to call her out for littering, but I could have handled it more respectfully and calmly. My approach was harsh, which led to her emotional reaction. So, in a way, I was partly right but also partly wrong in how I addressed the situation. Maybe the better approach would have been to politely explain why it's important to throw the peel in the trash, especially given the recent fly problem, instead of confronting her angrily. That way, I could have addressed the issue without making her feel attacked. So, in conclusion, while her action was wrong, my method of addressing it could have been improved. I was right to want to correct the behavior, but I was wrong in how I went about it.
